7.note: Applications closed. Requires school nomination (max 2 per school). Updated 2026 dates: July 1 – August 9. Stipend provided at conclusion. Apply in January of junior year for 2027.

8.cost: Free for families ≤$75k; scaled discounts up to ~$140k income; max ~$7,900
8.desc: One of the oldest and most prestigious STEM programs in the US (since 1959). Rising seniors spend 5 weeks doing authentic research in Astrophysics, Biochemistry, Bacterial Genomics, or Cell Biology (new track for 2026). Teams of 3, ~700 total spots across 16 campus sites. Need-blind admissions with generous financial aid — free for families ≤$75k household income, with sliding-scale discounts up to ~$140k. Alumni network of 4,300+ scientists and engineers.
8.note: 2026 domestic deadline was Feb 19 (international Jan 29). Free for families earning ≤$75k — threshold updated for 2026. Cell Biology is a new track added for 2026. Apply in junior year for 2027. SSP is comparable in prestige to RSI and MITES.

12.note: Deadline passed. 2026 dates: June 22 – August 3. Open to US citizens/permanent residents from underrepresented backgrounds. Fully funded — tuition, housing, meals, and stipend.

new_programs.name: NIH Summer Internship Program (SIP)
new_programs.loc: Bethesda, MD (NIH main campus) + satellite campuses
new_programs.desc: One of the most prestigious biomedical research internships available to high school students in the US. Graduating seniors (must be 18 by Sept 30, 2026 — or 17 by June 1 if within 40 miles of an NIH campus) conduct hands-on research with world-leading NIH scientists. Disciplines span cancer biology, genomics, neuroscience, immunology, clinical research, computational biology, and more. Students identify a PI, apply centrally, then proactively reach out to specific research groups. Paid stipend provided. Commuter program — no housing. US citizens/permanent residents only.
new_programs.note: 2026 application closed Feb 18. For high school seniors (graduating class 2026) only — must be 18 by Sept 30, 2026 (or 17 by June 1 if within 40 miles of NIH). After applying, students must proactively email NIH PIs — matching is self-directed. Apply for 2027: opens December, closes ~February. Among the most prestigious government research programs for young scientists.
new_programs.subject: Biomedical research across all NIH disciplines

new_programs.name: Rockefeller University Summer Science Research Program (SSRP)
new_programs.loc: New York City, NY (commuter — Upper East Side)
new_programs.desc: Highly selective free biomedical research internship at The Rockefeller University — a world-class institution with 26 Nobel Prize winners. ~25–30 rising juniors and seniors conduct authentic hands-on lab research under mentorship of Rockefeller scientists. Research spans biochemistry, cell biology, computational biology, genetics, immunology, neuroscience, and structural biology. Students present at a closing symposium. Must be at least 16 by program start. Commuter only — no housing. NYC-area students have a major practical advantage.
new_programs.note: 2026 application due Jan 2; letters of rec due Jan 5. Interviews in March; decisions in April. Apply for 2027 in December. Commuter only — no housing. One of the top research opportunities for NYC-area high schoolers and among the most prestigious in the country.
new_programs.subject: Biomedical and biological sciences research

new_programs.name: NIST Summer High School Internship Program (SHIP)
new_programs.host: National Institute of Standards and Technology
new_programs.loc: Gaithersburg, MD or Boulder, CO (commuter; must live within 50 miles)
new_programs.desc: Competitive 7-week unpaid research internship at NIST — the US federal measurement standards laboratory, home to Nobel laureates. Students work one-on-one with NIST staff scientists on cutting-edge projects in physics, chemistry, materials science, engineering, cybersecurity, quantum computing, and AI/ML. Must live within 50 miles of NIST Gaithersburg (MD) or NIST Boulder (CO). Commuter only. One of the most underrated government science programs for high schoolers.
new_programs.note: Strictly local — must live within 50 miles of NIST Gaithersburg, MD or NIST Boulder, CO. Unpaid but highly prestigious. Offers emailed March 30–April 21. Applications for 2027 open in mid-October at nist.gov/ship.
new_programs.subject: Physics, chemistry, materials science, engineering, cybersecurity, quantum computing, AI/ML

new_programs.name: Stanford AI4ALL
new_programs.host: Stanford Institute for Human-Centered AI (HAI) & Stanford Pre-Collegiate Studies
new_programs.cost: Program fee not publicly listed; need-based aid available
new_programs.desc: Prestigious 2-week AI immersion program for 9th graders only — one of the few elite STEM programs designed specifically for freshmen. Hosted by Stanford HAI and Stanford Pre-Collegiate Studies. Students explore AI through hands-on research projects in one of four tracks: Computer Vision, Medical AI, Natural Language Processing, or Robotics. Mentored by Stanford researchers and industry professionals. Available as fully online (June) or residential on-campus (July). No prior AI or programming experience required. Prioritizes underrepresented students in tech. Participants must be 14–15 years old during the program.
new_programs.note: 2026 application was due Feb 6; decisions by mid-April. ONLY for current 9th graders — not eligible if in grades 10–12. For 2027, apply in January at ai4all.spcs.stanford.edu. One of the most prestigious AI programs specifically targeting freshmen.
new_programs.subject: Artificial intelligence (Computer Vision, Medical AI, NLP, Robotics)

new_programs.name: Babson Summer Study – Entrepreneurship
new_programs.desc: World-ranked entrepreneurship experience at Babson College — consistently ranked the #1 undergraduate entrepreneurship school in the US. Students earn 4 transferable college credits through EPS 1110: Introduction to the Entrepreneurial Experience. Two tracks in 2026: AI-Enabled Entrepreneurship and Social Entrepreneurship. Students learn startup phases, market research, AI-driven product design, pitching, and go-to-market strategy. Classes run 8–11am ET; both online and residential formats offered.
new_programs.note: Still accepting for Summer 2026 — rolling admissions. Earns 4 transferable college credits. Two tracks: AI-Enabled Entrepreneurship or Social Entrepreneurship. Both online and in-person formats available.
new_programs.subject: Entrepreneurship, startup strategy, AI-enabled product design, go-to-market

new_programs.name: NYIF Young Finance Scholars
new_programs.loc: New York City, NY + Online (also Tokyo & London in-person options)
new_programs.dates: NYC In-Person: July 20–31, 2026 · Young Equity Analyst: Aug 10–21, 2026
new_programs.desc: Finance education program taught exclusively by active Wall Street professionals — not academics. The flagship 2-week Young Finance Scholars (NYC, ages 15–18, $1,990) covers financial markets, investment analysis, corporate finance, risk management, fintech, and ESG. The Young Equity Analyst program ($1,990) teaches real company valuation using DCF models and financial statement analysis. A self-paced online option ($950, ages 13–17) is also available. International sessions in Tokyo ($4,999) and London ($4,399). Strong portfolio piece for students targeting finance or economics careers.
new_programs.note: Still accepting for Summer 2026. All instructors are working Wall Street professionals. Best value entry point: self-paced online ($950). NYC in-person offers the deepest experience. International options available in Tokyo and London.
new_programs.subject: Financial markets, investment analysis, corporate finance, valuation, fintech, ESG
